title: Thoracoabdominal aortic aneurysms: Crawford classification, spinal protection and branch reconstruction
subject: ss-ctvs
refs: Sabiston Textbook of Surgery 22e Ch 113 (Thoracoabdominal Aortic Aneurysms)
2022 ACC/AHA Guideline for the Diagnosis and Management of Aortic Disease

steps.say: Thoracoabdominal aortic aneurysms span both the thoracic and abdominal cavities, posing tremendous surgical challenges. The Crawford classification categorizes them into five anatomical extents. Crawford extent two is the most surgically demanding, extending from the subclavian artery all the way to the aortic bifurcation.
steps.tx: The **Crawford classification** defines five anatomical extents of thoracoabdominal aneurysms. **Extent II** is the most complex and hazardous, extending from the left subclavian takeoff down to the aortoiliac bifurcation, carrying the highest baseline risks of **spinal cord ischemia** and renal failure.

rows: Suprarenal abdominal aorta above celiac axis
Infrarenal aorta down to aortic bifurcation
Infrarenal aorta down to aortic bifurcation
Involves total visceral aorta to bifurcation

steps.tx: The aorta in this view is aneurysmal in one continuous sweep, and the surgical problem changes with how far that sweep extends. Mapping the disease as **Crawford extents** from one to five tells the team which branch vessels, spinal cord protection and clamp strategy the repair will need. Extent two carries the heaviest burden because it spans nearly the whole descending and abdominal aorta in a single reconstruction.
steps.say: Crawford extents one to five map thoracoabdominal aneurysm length along the aorta. The extent dictates branch reconstruction, clamp strategy and spinal protection.

steps.say: Spinal cord ischemia and paraplegia are the most dreaded complications of thoracoabdominal repair. Sacrificing critical intercostal and lumbar arteries deprives the anterior spinal artery of blood flow. The artery of Adamkiewicz, typically arising between thoracic eight and lumbar one, is critical for cord perfusion.
steps.tx: Ischemic injury to the spinal cord produces catastrophic **paraplegia** in up to 10 percent of extensive repairs. Spinal infarction stems from sacrificing essential radicular feeders to the **anterior spinal artery**, most notably the major radicular **artery of Adamkiewicz** between T8 and L1.

nodes.label: Aortic cross-clamping and division of intercostal arteries
Acute reduction in anterior spinal artery perfusion pressure
Spinal cord ischemia exacerbated by elevated CSF pressure
Irreversible anterior horn motor neuron necrosis and paraplegia

steps.say: A multimodal spinal cord protection protocol significantly reduces paraplegia rates. Cerebrospinal fluid drainage lowers intrathecal pressure below ten millimeters of mercury, improving spinal cord perfusion. Perfusionists also keep mean arterial pressure above eighty and utilize mild systemic hypothermia.
steps.tx: Modern surgical protocols employ a **multimodal spinal protection** bundle. Inserting a preoperative **cerebrospinal fluid drain** maintains intrathecal pressure strictly below 10 mmHg. Surgeons combine this with permissive mild hypothermia and actively target a **mean arterial pressure > 80 mmHg** to drive collateral cord blood flow.

rows: Augments spinal cord perfusion gradient (MAP minus CSFP)
Drives collateral flow through vertebral and hypogastric beds
Passive systemic cool to 32 to 34 C
Suppresses neuronal metabolic rate and oxygen consumption

steps.say: Distal aortic perfusion maintains oxygenated blood flow to the lower body during cross-clamping. Surgeons establish left heart bypass from the left atrium to the common femoral artery using a centrifugal pump. This maintains mesenteric, renal, and spinal collateral perfusion while the proximal anastomosis is sewn.
steps.tx: Employing **left heart bypass** from the left atrium or left pulmonary vein to the common femoral artery ensures continuous **distal aortic perfusion**. This circuit delivers oxygenated blood to the spinal collateral network and kidneys, mitigating severe **visceral ischemic injury** during proximal aortic clamping.

nodes.label: Cannulate left atrium and left common femoral artery
Deploy centrifugal pump without systemic heparinization
Cross-clamp thoracic aorta to begin proximal repair
Maintain distal perfusion pressure > 60 mmHg to viscera

steps.say: Neurophysiological monitoring detects intraoperative spinal cord ischemia in real time. Motor-evoked potentials monitor the integrity of the anterior corticospinal motor tracts. A loss of motor amplitudes indicates that the surgical team must reimplant critical intercostal vessels immediately.
steps.tx: Intraoperative neurophysiological surveillance utilizing **motor-evoked potentials** provides real-time monitoring of anterior spinal motor tract perfusion. A greater than 50 percent drop in amplitude signals impending **spinal ischemia**, prompting immediate **intercostal reimplantation** and mean arterial pressure elevation to reverse motor pathway injury.

left.title: Motor-Evoked Potentials (MEPs)
points: Assesses anterior corticospinal tract and anterior horn cells
Highly sensitive to acute anterior spinal artery ischemia
Instantaneous feedback during cross-clamping and vessel division

right.title: Somatosensory-Evoked Potentials (SSEPs)
points: Assesses posterior columns fed by dual posterior spinal arteries
Lacks sensitivity for isolated anterior motor pathway infarction
Exhibits a substantial latency delay of 15 to 30 minutes

steps.say: Protecting renal function requires active cold preservation during visceral ischemia. Teams infuse cold crystalloid preservation solutions with mannitol or methylprednisolone into both renal artery ostia through catheter perfusion. Cold perfusion drops parenchymal temperature to fifteen degrees, protecting nephrons.
steps.tx: To prevent acute kidney injury during visceral clamping, surgeons initiate selective **cold renal perfusion**. Catheters deliver 4 degrees Celsius crystalloid flush containing **mannitol** and corticosteroids directly into both renal ostia, providing robust **hypothermic renal protection** throughout the ischemic period. Rapidly lowering parenchymal temperature suppresses tubular cell metabolic breakdown and preserves glomerular architecture throughout the visceral cross-clamp phase.

rows: Induces rapid parenchymal hypothermia, halting ATP breakdown
Reduces endothelial swelling and scavenges free oxygen radicals
Continuous blood perfusion via 9 Fr lines
Active metabolic maintenance during extended branch reconstruction

steps.say: Visceral branch reconstruction will connect the celiac axis, superior mesenteric artery, and both renal arteries. In the Carrel patch technique, branches are reimplanted as a single composite aortic island into the Dacron graft. Alternatively, separate branched Dacron grafts allow individual bypass to each visceral artery.
steps.tx: Reconstruction of visceral vessels employs an inclusion **Carrel patch** incorporating the celiac axis, superior mesenteric, and right renal arteries into a common aortic cuff. When aortic tissue is diseased or ectatic, surgeons select **branched Dacron grafts** with individual bypass limbs to achieve **visceral revascularization**.

left.title: Inclusion Carrel Patch
points: Reimplants celiac, SMA, and right renal as single island
Rapid completion time minimizes visceral clamp duration
Prone to late patch aneurysmal degeneration in connective disorders

right.title: Multi-Branched Graft (Coselli / Individual)
points: Separate 8 to 10 mm prosthetic limbs sewn to each visceral branch
Completely eliminates all native diseased aortic tissue
Technically demanding with longer cumulative ischemic times

steps.say: Advanced endovascular options have revolutionized management in high-risk patients. Fenestrated and branched endovascular repair deploys custom-manufactured stent grafts with dedicated visceral branches. This closed approach avoids thoracophrenolaparotomy and reduces operative blood loss.
steps.tx: For elderly or physiologically frail patients, **fenestrated-branched TEVAR** offers an advanced endovascular alternative to open thoracophrenolaparotomy. Custom stent grafts with reinforced fenestrations maintain visceral branch patency, achieving significantly lower early **perioperative mortality** in **high-risk surgical patients** with favorable landing zones.
